inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 tanshin (year ended 2026-03-31) statement of changes in equity: share-based payment transactions JPY 47m (line 764) -- immaterial, treated as zero; SBC-zero market
inputs.fy_label_note: CSV labels by END year: FY2026 = year ended 2026-03-31, which the company calls 'FY2025'. Forecast year FY2027 (ending 2027-03-31) is the company's 'FY2026'.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T06:30:00Z regular TSE close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.share_count_basis: 290,814,015 issued less 22,326,154 treasury at 2026-06-30 = 268,487,861 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin). Diluted EPS equals basic (no dilutive instruments). Held FLAT: SBC is nil, and the ongoing buyback (JPY 15.0bn FY2026, JPY 20.0bn in Q1 FY2027 alone) is not credited with further count reduction.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built: 10y JGB ~1.9%, ERP 5.5%, beta 1.3 (diversified copper/nickel/gold miner-smelter) -> cost of equity ~9.1%; after-tax cost of debt ~0.9% (AA- JCR, yen bonds); 75/25 equity/debt at current market cap gives a mechanical ~7.0-7.5%. House reference for JPY industrials is ~9%. 8.0% is the midpoint of the two, used in ALL three scenarios -- commodity cyclicality is charged in the scenario paths and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Interest-bearing debt (bonds + borrowings, JPY 714,651m at 2026-06-30) EXCLUDES lease liabilities per the Integrated Report (note 2 to the financial-position page). Lease cash is small (financing 'other' JPY 4.2bn FY2026) and is charged inside the flows at 0.3% of revenue; lease liabilities are not in net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: NCI (JPY 225.9bn book at 2026-06-30, mainly Taganito/Coral Bay HPAL minorities) took 5-7% of profit in normal years (FY2026: 12.4bn of 188.7bn). Folded into the 30% combined cash-tax-and-leakage rate (effective tax ~26% on FY2026 PBT, equity-method income already post-tax, plus ~4pp NCI leakage). No NCI deduction in the bridge. Calibration: FY0 (EBITDA 278.2 - lease ~5 - D&A 59.8) x 0.70 = JPY 149bn vs attributable NI 176.3bn less ~28bn after-tax net finance income = ~148bn -- ties.
inputs.ebitda_definition: CSV EBITDA = profit before tax - finance income + finance costs + D&A. It therefore INCLUDES share of profit of equity-method mines (JPY 40.6bn FY2026; Cerro Verde, Quebrada Blanca etc.) and EXCLUDES all finance income (interest on JV shareholder loans and dividends on cross-shareholdings). The source assets of the excluded income are added in equity_bridge (matching-asset rule); equity-method investments (JPY 566.7bn) are NOT added because their income is in the flows.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (JPY WACC, lease treatment B, NCI folded into leakage, matching-asset bridge, SBC-zero). Chosen because SMM is an operating miner/smelter/materials company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; no bank/REIT/holdco characteristics. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). Owner FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF 16,219 - SBC 0 - interest received 42,547 = -26,328 (FY2026). Interest income is stripped because it is interest on ~JPY 550bn of shareholder loans to JV mines (Mineral Resources segment finance income JPY 46.9bn), not on the cash pile; those loans and the JPY ~349bn cross-shareholding portfolio are added to the bridge at book instead. Reported FCF history is weak (avg JPY ~53bn FY2019-FY2026) because of the QB/Cote capex supercycle, metal-price-driven inventory build and JV lending; the forward build assumes the investment program is past peak (JCR, May 2026) and working capital stops absorbing cash at the mid-cycle. Mid-cycle normalization: year-1 margin follows the August 2026 guidance, then margins revert from a copper $12.7k/t, gold $4.2k/oz, JPY 160 world toward a ~14% EBITDA margin (FY2019-FY2026 average ex the FY2022 super-year and the FY2025 impairment) by year 3. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (count held flat); the company IS a repurchaser.

equity_bridge.item: Non-current other financial assets at book (JV shareholder loans ~JPY 550bn earning the stripped interest income, plus cross-shareholdings ~JPY 349bn at fair value incl. PTVI)
equity_bridge.note: Q1 FY2027 tanshin statement of financial position, 2026-06-30 (line 414). Matching asset for the excluded finance income. Recoverability of the Quebrada Blanca loans is the main risk to this line.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: long-run volume growth (QB/Cote ramp, nickel matte furnace) plus yen inflation. The 5-year equity CAGR of 13.3% is measured from the FY2021 trough to a record-price FY2026 and is not a forward rate for a commodity producer.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 13.3% agrees with revenue (13.5%) and EPS (13.5%) -- no divergence between them -- but all three are trough-to-peak. Owner FCF is NEGATIVE in FY2023 (-21.6bn) and FY2026 (-26.3bn) once interest on JV loans is stripped, so FCF CAGRs are undefined: reported growth has been funded by the capex supercycle and JV lending, not converted to cash.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF - interest received): FY2019 61.0, FY2020 85.0, FY2021 47.0, FY2022 99.4, FY2023 -21.6, FY2024 50.7, FY2025 -16.9, FY2026 -26.3 (JPY bn). Mid-cycle attributable net income FY2019-FY2026 ~JPY 125bn/yr (~JPY 465/share on the current count).

base.growth_note: Y1 = August 2026 revised guidance (net sales JPY 2,065bn, +18.6%). Y2-Y3 give back part of the price windfall as copper/gold/JPY revert toward mid-cycle; thereafter 2.5% volume + inflation.
base.margin_note: Y1 17.0% is guidance-implied (PBT 324bn - net finance income ~37bn + D&A ~70bn = ~357bn, 17.3%); reverts to the 14% FY2019-FY2026 average ex FY2022 and ex the FY2025 impairment by Y4.
base.capex_note: 3-Year Plan 2027 capex + investment JPY 540bn (~180bn/yr incl. JV lending); PPE+intangibles cash capex ran 8-9% of revenue FY2023-FY2025 and 4.9% in FY2026. 7.5% Y1 covers the plan's last heavy year and the Rio Tinto JV / Winu / Kalgoorlie feasibility spend; glides to 5% as the program passes peak. D&A 3.5% (FY2026 3.4%).
base.tax_note: 30% = ~26% effective cash tax (equity-method income is post-tax) + ~4pp NCI leakage.
base.wc_note: Negative capture: a smelter carries metal inventory and receivables that scale with price x volume (FY2026 WC absorbed JPY 172bn on +148bn revenue). -15% of the revenue change is the through-cycle rate; it releases cash in the Y2-Y3 revenue decline.

bull.narrative: Copper supercycle holds ($12-13k/t), gold stays above $4k, yen stays weak; margins hold near the FY2021-FY2023 level rather than reverting.

bear.narrative: Copper reverts to ~$9k/t, gold to ~$3k, yen to ~140; nickel glut persists; TC/RC stay near zero; Materials losses recur; QB tailings fix slips -- margins fall to the FY2024-FY2025 level and stay there.

scenario_narratives.base: Year 1 follows the August 2026 upgrade (copper $12,706/t, nickel $7.68/lb, gold $4,204/oz, JPY 159.87/$ for the full year; Q1 already delivered JPY 118bn PBT). From year 2 the model treats those prices as cyclically high rather than structural: revenue gives back ~9% over two years and the EBITDA margin settles at 14%, the FY2019-FY2026 average once the FY2022 super-year and the FY2025 HPAL impairment are excluded. Volume growth from Quebrada Blanca reaching stable operation (232-265kt in 2027 on a 100% basis), Cote Gold at 12-13.6t and the nickel matte furnace (end FY2027) lifts revenue 2.5%/yr thereafter. Capex glides from the 3-Year Plan 2027 peak (JPY 540bn over three years including JV financing) toward 5% of revenue, and working capital stops absorbing cash once metal prices stop rising. The JV shareholder loans and cross-shareholdings are carried in the bridge at book.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI/grid-electrification copper story is structural: copper holds $12-13k/t, gold stays above $4k, the yen stays near 160 and Indonesia's ore-quota cuts plus Middle East sulfur constraints tighten nickel. Toyo's own-mine concentrate ratio rises toward 80%, neutralising the TC/RC squeeze; Quebrada Blanca clears its tailings constraint on schedule; Materials recovers on ESS and data-center demand (SiC, scandium for SOFCs). Margins hold at 16.5% (between the FY2021 and FY2023 levels) and revenue never gives back the FY2027 step-up. The equity ratio above 58% funds continued buybacks, which the flat count does not credit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Copper reverts to ~$9,000/t and gold to ~$3,000/oz as the AI capex cycle cools and China's property demand stays weak; the yen appreciates to ~140 on BoJ normalisation, cutting yen-translated metal revenue. Indonesian nickel keeps the market in surplus (SMM's own forecast runs surplus through 2026), copper TC/RC stay at historic lows so Smelting & Refining earns little, and battery-material product changeovers plus LFP substitution keep Materials near breakeven. Quebrada Blanca's tailings fix slips and more capex is needed; the 3-Year Plan capex is not past peak. Revenue falls ~19% over two years and the EBITDA margin settles at 11%, the FY2024-FY2025 underlying level. JV loan recoverability becomes a live question.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default): copper and gold are at or near record highs and the yen near its weakest, so a mean-reversion path is at least as likely as its continuation; management itself says a large share of the recent profit improvement is price and one-offs. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs copper, gold, the yen and nickel to all stay favourable at once, and a demonstrated QB fix. No going-concern or refinancing risk (58.7% equity ratio, AA- stable), so the bear is not weighted higher than 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A commodity producer is valued on mid-cycle cash generation, not on the current price deck. The August 2026 guidance is honoured in year 1 and then faded; the structural improvements (new mines at full rate, higher own-mine ratio, nickel matte) are what justify a mid-cycle margin at the historical average rather than below it. The large financial-asset block (JV shareholder loans and cross-shareholdings) is carried at book in the bridge with its income excluded from the flows, so the valuation is not double-counting the JV cash stream.
key_risks_to_valuation: Copper/gold/JPY reversal: every 1pp of sustained EBITDA margin is worth roughly JPY 500-600/share at the base revenue level; the bear path is a 3pp lower terminal margin
Recoverability of the ~JPY 550bn of shareholder loans to JV mines (Quebrada Blanca) carried at book in the bridge -- a 20% haircut is ~JPY 410/share
Capex overrun: the 3-Year Plan already rose from JPY 437bn to 540bn; a further year at 8-9% of revenue removes ~JPY 50bn of FCF
Working capital: a renewed metal-price surge absorbs cash into inventory (FY2026: JPY 172bn), so the 'bull' earnings path converts to cash later than the model assumes
Nickel: Indonesian supply keeps the HPAL/ferronickel chain and Materials near breakeven; a further impairment at Coral Bay/Taganito is possible
NCI and tax leakage modelled as a flat 30%; if the HPAL minorities' share of profit rises (nickel recovery), attributable flows are lower than modelled
